external_research.title: How Do Transformers Learn Variable Binding in Symbolic Programs?
external_research.relevance: Reports a training trajectory from random prediction to a shallow heuristic and then a systematic variable-binding mechanism; motivates checkpoint-separated developmental diagnostics rather than final accuracy alone.

external_research.title: Rectifying Demonstration Shortcut in In-Context Learning
external_research.relevance: Shows that ICL can rely on pretrained semantic priors of demonstrations rather than the input-label relation, including tasks with semantically unrelated labels; motivates opaque remapping and shortcut controls.

external_research.title: Enhancing Input-Label Mapping in In-Context Learning with Contrastive Decoding
external_research.relevance: Provides additional evidence that input-label mapping is a distinct failure surface in ICL; supports explicit BIND/ROUTE evaluation instead of treating overall task success as binding evidence.

external_research.title: Steering the Language Axis: From Linear Decodability to Causal Control
external_research.relevance: Causal activation steering is layer- and direction-dependent across model families; supports exact model/runtime/site binding and blocks transfer of raw activation-coordinate labels across layers or models.

external_research.title: Navigating Shortcuts, Spurious Correlations, and Confounders: From Origins via Detection to Mitigation
external_research.relevance: Unifies shortcut/confounder failure classes and supports model-visible nuisance challenge tests rather than relying on marginal balance alone.

hypotheses.hypothesis: A Qwen3.5-0.8B cognitive module can learn episode-local semantic-to-opaque-symbol binding as a reusable process, but may pass through a shortcut/heuristic phase before systematic binding emerges.
hypotheses.counterhypothesis: Observed progress can be fully explained by surface priors, codebook/display-order shortcuts or memorized mapping families without a reusable binder.
hypotheses.discriminator: Checkpoint-separated READ/BIND/WRITE curves on family-disjoint unseen mappings, unseen display orders, nuisance-ablation signatures, full S3 orbit consistency and distractor-depth stress; require systematic gains without retention collapse.
hypotheses.promotion_rule: Do not promote BIND/ROUTE competence from aggregate accuracy or one final checkpoint.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Semantic Hyperposition can remain the carrier-independent training target while any activation/J-Space coordinate control stays model/runtime/site-specific.
hypotheses.counterhypothesis: A discovered activation direction is globally transferable and can be used directly as a cross-layer or cross-model semantic label.
hypotheses.discriminator: Exact checkpoint/tokenizer/runtime/site controls with sign-flip, null, same-norm orthogonal/permuted, off-target, lesion/rescue and disjoint semantic holdout; test site transfer explicitly rather than assuming it.
hypotheses.promotion_rule: Raw activation coordinates remain blocked as portable labels without exact causal evidence.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Model-visible semantic ablation plus exact nuisance-signature grouping is a stronger shortcut detector for the Trigger-2 binder than hidden audit metadata or marginal mutual-information checks alone.
hypotheses.counterhypothesis: Marginal counterbalancing already suffices and higher-order visible nuisance combinations add no shortcut capacity.
hypotheses.discriminator: Require full-cross or preregistered conditional-independence design, nuisance-only exact-signature decoder at prior performance, and rejection after injecting a visible target-correlated nuisance tag.
hypotheses.promotion_rule: Keep binding_router_factorial_generator_v3 blocked from direct training until rendered-byte successor gates pass.
